title: Regularity and boundary intersections persist under sufficiently fine marked approximation
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be an excellent henselian Noetherian local domain, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $\widehat S=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$ [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Write $\widehat A=\varinjlim_\alpha A_\alpha$ as its directed union of finite type $A$-subalgebras, and let $s_\alpha:A_\alpha\to\widehat A$ be the inclusions. Let $Z\subset S$ be closed and let $X_i\to\widehat S$ be finitely many finite type morphisms, with $X_i$ regular Noetherian and $Z\times_SX_i$ supported on a strict normal crossings boundary $D_i$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. There is an index $\alpha_0$ and a finite diagram of finite type schemes over $S_{\alpha_0}=\operatorname{Spec}A_{\alpha_0}$ whose base change is the diagram consisting of all $X_i$, the reduced irreducible components of each $D_i$, all their scheme-theoretic intersections, and their inclusions. After increasing $\alpha_0$, there is $N_0\geq1$ such that for every $\alpha\geq\alpha_0$, every $N\geq N_0$ and every $A$-algebra map $u:A_\alpha\to A$ congruent to $s_\alpha$ modulo $\mathfrak m^N\widehat A$, the pulled-back model $X_{i,u}$ has an open neighborhood $V_{i,u}$ of its entire closed fibre which is regular, on which the pulled-back markings form a strict normal crossings boundary supported on $Z\times_S V_{i,u}$. On $V_{i,u}$ the reduced union of the irreducible components of $X_{i,u}$ dominating $S$ is an open and closed subscheme. All intersections at points of this neighborhood have the expected local codimensions. Empty boundaries and empty intersections are permitted. The models may be enlarged to include any specified finite diagram of finite type schemes and morphisms involving the $X_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Expose III section 2 (pp.35--36), Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.4 (pp.41--43), and the final paragraph of the proof of Proposition 6.2 (pp.44--45). Include every boundary intersection before approximation; regular local dimensions and cotangent dimensions persist by 5.4, giving codimensions by excellence/catenarity. This is the finite marked-diagram consequence stated in that paragraph, not the uniformization reduction itself.
